rows.citation: Wehling L, Singh G, Mulyadi AW, et al. (2025). Talk2Biomodels: AI agent-based open-source LLM initiative for kinetic biological models. bioRxiv (preprint); peer-reviewed version in BMC Bioinformatics 26:276 (2025), doi:10.1186/s12859-025-06310-1.
rows.model_type: SBML kinetic ODE models from BioModels (systems biology); not neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: no; users can change parameters and run parameter scans through natural language, but there are no recorded single-fault mutants or mutation operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; offers time-course simulation, parameter scans and steady-state analysis, not batteries of current-clamp stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; outputs are species time courses, steady states and annotations; no voltage or spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; no selection of tests or protocols for detecting faults or behavioural change.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial; the agent is benchmarked on synthetic question-answer sets (312 pairs) using LLM-as-judge task completion, not on held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: partial; an LLM agent retrieves, simulates, re-parameterises and saves SBML models, but whether its edits preserve model behaviour is not tested.
rows.software: Talk2Biomodels, part of AIAgents4Pharma (MIT per GitHub API and LICENSE file; latest release v1.49.1) https://github.com/VirtualPatientEngine/AIAgents4Pharma
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: T2B is a conversational agent for exploring and simulating SBML models, evaluated on task completion. NeuroSem targets NeuroML neuron models and tests whether edits preserve electrophysiological behaviour, using mutation-calibrated, optimised protocol batteries with held-out evaluation. T2B is relevant only to NeuroSem's secondary AI-agent case study.
rows.verification_method: Crossref (preprint and published DOI); bioRxiv API (details and pubs: published_doi 10.1186/s12859-025-06310-1, BMC Bioinformatics, 2025-11-18); Europe PMC abstract and full text PMC12625589 (methods, benchmarking, availability); GitHub API via gh plus raw LICENSE and README for AIAgents4Pharma.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:biorxiv.org (LLM computational neuroscience model building agent automated modeling) | Europe PMC LLM/AI agent + SBML query; verified via Crossref + abstract

rows.citation: Sinha A, Gleeson P, Pandey A, et al. (2026). NeuroML/pyNeuroML: v1.3.22. Zenodo.
rows.model_type: general tooling for NeuroML2/LEMS neuron and network models (reading, writing, validating, simulating, exporting)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; provides validation, simulation and export functions, but no mutation generation or fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; the analysis helper generate_current_vs_frequency_curve simulates a cell over a range of step current amplitudes.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; produces firing-rate (IF) and IV curves, and analyse_spiketime_vs_dt compares spike times across time steps; no eFEL-style feature battery.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; a 'tune' extra exists for parameter tuning or fitting, but nothing selects stimulation protocols for fault detection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; this is a software release, not an evaluation study.
rows.software: pyNeuroML v1.3.22 (LGPL-3.0-only per PyPI and DataCite; GitHub latest release v1.3.22, 2026-06-02) https://github.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML; Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5744044
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A core dependency, not a competitor. NeuroSem would call validators.validate_neuroml2, run_lems_with_jneuroml and the jNeuroML exports, and add single-fault mutants, multi-protocol eFEL fingerprints, dt-refinement tolerance calibration, greedy protocol selection and held-out evaluation. analyse_spiketime_vs_dt is a partial precedent for the refinement step.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API for 10.5281/zenodo.20513275 (title, creators, version, license, IsVersionOf concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5744044); PyPI JSON (1.3.22, LGPL-3.0-only); GitHub API via gh (license, latest release); raw README, pyneuroml/validators.py, runners.py and analysis/__init__.py from GitHub master.
rows.found_via: OpenAlex search 'pyNeuroML' | GitHub org:NeuroML search + DOI badge in pyNeuroML README; DataCite API; PyPI JSON (pyneuroml 1.3.22) | OpenAlex search 'pyNeuroML' (work W7163174990); PyPI JSON API https://pypi.org/pypi/pyNeuroML/json (1.3.22, LGPL-3.0-only); Zenodo API timed out

rows.citation: Marin B, Gleeson P, Cantarelli M, et al. (2014). Automated code generation from LEMS, the general purpose model specification language underpinning NeuroML2. BMC Neuroscience 15(Suppl 1):P45.
rows.model_type: LEMS/NeuroML2 hybrid dynamical systems; single-cell models translated to C (Sundials), XPPAUT, MATLAB and Modelica
rows.controlled_mutations: no; a conference abstract describing code generators, with no fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear; the abstract reports runnable single-cell simulations on several platforms but describes no stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; no feature extraction or quantitative output comparison is described.
rows.ai_transformations: no; translation uses deterministic, template-based generators working from a flattened, dimensionless intermediate format (dLEMS).
rows.software: unclear; the abstract says the tools are open source but gives no repository URL in the retrieved text
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Describes the kind of LEMS-to-simulator translation NeuroSem aims to test, and reports only that the generated simulations run. NeuroSem would check whether such translations preserve behaviour, using multi-protocol feature comparison with refinement-calibrated tolerances and seeded faults.
rows.verification_method: Crossref (title, authors, BMC Neuroscience vol 15 suppl S1, P45, 2014-07); Europe PMC full text PMC4126487 (CNS*2014 abstract body read).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org large language model generate computational neuroscience model code NEURON Brian (PMC link); verified via Crossref | Europe PMC citations of NeuroML 2010 (PMC4126487); Crossref-verified

rows.citation: Ranjan R, Van Geit W, Moor R, et al. (2026). eFEL (version 5.7.23). Zenodo.
rows.model_type: electrophysiology feature extraction from voltage traces (in vitro and in silico)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; an analysis library with no model mutation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; it extracts features from traces the user supplies and does not design or run stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes; extracts user-selected features such as action-potential amplitude and width (C++ core, Python wrapper).
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; this is a software record.
rows.software: eFEL (LGPL per LICENSE.txt, with examples and tests BSD; LGPL-3.0-only in DataCite) https://github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL; PyPI and GitHub latest release 5.7.34
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A dependency NeuroSem would reuse for fingerprint features. NeuroSem adds protocol execution, tolerance calibration, mutants, protocol selection and held-out evaluation. Note: this DOI is the v5.7.23 record, while the current release is 5.7.34. The README asks users to cite Mandge et al. (2026), Bioinformatics 42(6), doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btag328 (Crossref-verified).
rows.verification_method: DataCite API for 10.5281/zenodo.19631743 (title 'eFEL', v5.7.23, creators, issued 2026-04-17, LGPL-3.0-only, IsVersionOf 10.5281/zenodo.19604220, whose DataCite record lists HasVersion links); PyPI JSON (5.7.34); GitHub API via gh (latest release 5.7.34); raw README and LICENSE.txt; Crossref for the eFEL Bioinformatics paper.
rows.found_via: OpenAlex search 'Electrophys Feature Extraction Library eFEL' (many Zenodo version DOIs returned, including an older 'eFEL 2.6' record 10.5281/zenodo.30074 dated 2015)

rows.citation: Gewaltig M-O, Cannon R (2014). Current Practice in Software Development for Computational Neuroscience and How to Improve It. PLoS Computational Biology 10(1):e1003376.
rows.model_type: general computational neuroscience software (simulators and tools); review and position paper
rows.controlled_mutations: no; a review of development practice with no testing experiments.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; qualitative categorisation of software projects.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background and motivation only. It categorises software development practice, proposes quality checklists, and notes that computational neuroscience has few standard tests (Rallpack cited as an exception, contrasted with the SBML test suite). NeuroSem targets one concrete gap: behavioural regression testing of neuron-model transformations.
rows.verification_method: Crossref (title, authors, PLoS Comput Biol 10(1) e1003376, 2014-01-23); Europe PMC abstract and full text PMC3900372 (keyword reading on testing and validation passages).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:dl.acm.org software testing practices computational neuroscience simulators (arXiv link); verified via Crossref | Europe PMC citations of NeuroML 2010

rows.citation: Tikidji-Hamburyan RA, Narayana V, Bozkus Z, et al. (2017). Software for Brain Network Simulations: A Comparative Study. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 11:46.
rows.model_type: spiking network models (a LIF PING network and a Hodgkin-Huxley PIR-ING network) implemented in NEURON, GENESIS, BRIAN and NEST
rows.controlled_mutations: no; the same models are implemented by hand in each simulator, with no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; two network case studies with fixed drive (for example Poisson input), not stimulation protocol batteries.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; compares network activity through raster plots and oscillation behaviour; no single-cell electrophysiological feature extraction.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; a comparative benchmark of model range, performance, parallelism and usability.
rows.software: unclear; implementation code location not checked
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A cross-simulator comparison that found similar but non-identical network activity for identically parameterised models, and left the cause open. NeuroSem would instead quantify behavioural divergence of single-cell NeuroML transformations against calibrated tolerances, using controlled mutants and optimised protocols. Relevant background for the optional cross-simulator extension.
rows.verification_method: Crossref (title, authors, Front Neuroinform vol 11, article 46, 2017-07-20); Europe PMC abstract and full text PMC5517781 (case-study and results passages).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:dl.acm.org software testing practices computational neuroscience simulators (PMC link); verified via Crossref | Europe PMC citations of NeuroML 2010 and ModelDB 2004
